title: Poly Pizza
description: Explore and download stylized 3D models for use in XR and game development.
educational: Students can search and incorporate free-to-use 3D assets into XR, game design, or digital art projects.

title: Hubs (Hubs Foundation)
description: Create shared 3D spaces for meetings, events, or educational walkthroughs — all in your browser.
educational: Great for virtual classrooms, student collaboration, and presentations in immersive environments.
notes: Mozilla ended official support for Hubs on May 31, 2024. This community-run instance from the Hubs Foundation is the current continuation of the project.

title: Sketchfab
description: Browse millions of interactive 3D models and view them in WebXR-enabled browsers.
educational: Art and science instructors can use Sketchfab to embed and explore 3D structures and artworks.

title: SculptGL
description: Free browser-based 3D sculpting app — like a virtual clay studio.
educational: Students can experiment with form and shape using virtual sculpting tools from any device.

title: SuperSplat
description: A free, open-source, browser-based editor for viewing, cleaning up, annotating, and publishing 3D Gaussian Splats -- no install required. Built by PlayCanvas.
educational: Great for showing students how real-world scenes captured by phone or drone become navigable 3D scenes; supports guided tours with annotations and camera viewpoints, and publishes directly to WebXR for VR/AR viewing.
notes: Drag and drop a .ply Gaussian Splat file to start editing. MIT licensed.

title: Smithsonian 3D Digitization
tags: 3D Models, Museum Collections, Open Access, AR
description: Browse and explore thousands of 3D-scanned Smithsonian objects in your browser, from dinosaur fossils and space artifacts to historical garments and cultural heritage pieces, all free to view, download, and reuse.
educational: A strong cross-curricular resource: science classes can examine fossils and spacecraft, history and social studies classes can explore artifacts and cultural heritage objects, and art classes can study 3D-scanned sculptures and design pieces. Many objects support AR viewing directly in the browser.
notes: Content spans the Smithsonian's museums (Natural History, Air and Space, American History, and more). Uses the open-source Voyager viewer.

title: WebGL Gaussian Splat Viewer
description: A lightweight, open-source WebGL viewer for exploring pre-captured 3D Gaussian Splat scenes (gardens, statues, vehicles, and more) directly in the browser, with keyboard, mouse, touch, and gamepad navigation.
educational: A simple, no-signup way to demonstrate what Gaussian Splatting is and let students navigate a real captured 3D scene, without needing the more involved SuperSplat editor.
notes: One of the earliest and most widely cited browser Gaussian Splat viewers. The author now points to the newer Spark renderer (sparkjs.dev) for more advanced projects.
